kp_title: KP 1. Applying the Definition of the Double Integral in Terms of Lower and Upper Riemann Sums
raw_html:
1.?

Let R=[1,3]×[−2,−1] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y)=10+y−3x. Further, let

I=∬Rf(x,y)dA

be the unique number such that over all rectangular partitions P of R, we have L(f,P)≤I≤U(f,P), where L(f,P) and U(f,P) are the corresponding lower and upper Riemann sums, and

U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1nAAAAAΔxiΔyj.

What expression is missing from the double summation above?

kp_title: KP 3. Calculating a Double Integral Using the Mean Value of X and Y
raw_html:
11.?

Let R=[−4,0]×[−5,−2] be a region in the xy-plane, and let f(x,y) be a function defined over R. The lower and upper Riemann sums corresponding to an arbitrary partition P of R are given by L(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(−2xi−5yj)ΔxiΔyj,U(f,P)=∑i=1m∑j=1n(−2xi−1−5yj−1)ΔxiΔyj.

Using the definition of the double integral in terms of L(f,P) and U(f,P), compute ∬Rf(x,y)dA.

Hint: You may wish to make use of the following result: ∑i=1m∑j=1n(xi−1+xi)ΔxiΔyj=(xm2−x02)(yn−y0)
